la:noun:solstitium.html:
solstĭtĭum, ii, n.
sol-sisto
.
In gen., the time when the sun seems to stand still, either in Cancer or in Capricorn, the (summer or winter) solstice (so in gen. not till after the Aug. period): solstitium aestivum ... hibernum,: aestivum,: brumale,: solstitia et aequinoctia,.—
In partic., the summer solstice, the longest day of the year (opp. bruma, the prevalent signif. of the word): alter motus solis est ... a brumā ad solstitium. Solstitium quod sol eo die sistere videbatur, Müll.; ; ; ; ; ; ; ; —
Transf., in gen., summer time, the heat of summer (poet. and in post-Aug. prose; cf. bruma, 2.): paenula solstitio, campestre nivalibus auris ; ; ; : solstitium pecori defendite,.

la:adj:solstitialis.html:
solstĭtĭālis, e, adj.
solstitium
.
Lit., of or belonging to the summer solstice, solstitial (opp. brumalis): (sol) Brumales adeat flexus, atque inde revortens Cancri se ut vortat metas ad solstitiales,: dies,the day on which the sun enters Cancer, the longest day,: tempus,; : nox,i. e. the shortest,: ortus sideris,: circulus,the tropic of Cancer, Müll.; .—Called also orbis, : exortus,the point where the sun rises at the summer solstice,.—
Transf.
Of or belonging to midsummer or summer heat: herba, i. e. a summer plant or one that quickly withers, ; ; : spinae,: acini,: tempus, Drak.: caput Leonis,: morbus,the midsummer fever,.—
Of or belonging to the sun, solar (for solaris): annus, qui solstitiali circumagitur orbe,in a solar revolution,; for which, annus,: plaga,i. e. the south,.
